title: A Simple Exercise Program For Teachers
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin lays out a minimalist home exercise program designed specifically for busy teachers who lack time or motivation for a gym routine. His core principles include exercising at home to eliminate commute time, working out every single day to cement the habit rather than aiming for a few sessions a week, starting with just minutes at a time, favoring brief interval-style calisthenics over long cardio sessions, and limiting each day to just two or three exercises using only body weight. He advises giving only about 75 percent effort rather than pushing to exhaustion, arguing that consistency, not intensity, is what produces lasting results. He frames small, unglamorous, daily action as far more effective than dramatic New Year's resolutions.
points: Recommends exercising at home to eliminate commute time, which he identifies as the biggest reason people quit within three months.
Advises exercising every single day rather than a few times a week, arguing daily repetition is what actually builds the habit.
Favors brief interval-style calisthenics over long cardio sessions, citing research on efficiency and fat-burning benefits.
Suggests giving only about 75 percent effort to keep the experience sustainable rather than punishing.
Frames small, consistent daily action, not dramatic New Year's resolutions, as the real driver of lasting change.
quotes: While it’s true that leaving home to exercise can be an initial motivator, eventually it becomes your biggest hurdle and a reason why more than 90% of people quit within three months.

But the truth is, fewer is harder because it never really becomes a habit. Exercising every day, on the other hand, is the easiest way to make it part of your lifestyle and eventually something you look forward to.
Interval training, on the other hand, which entails short bursts of exercise followed by rest, gives you more bang for your buck. Every study supports this.
The way to ensure you’re doing this is to give only 75% of your best effort.
Big results don’t come from big, dramatic changes—which are destined to fail. They come from small, quiet changes barely noticeable and repeated over time.
Before you know it, your daily workout will become a habit you can’t live without.
